meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Thin file: neutral Te has little modern precision spectroscopy in open sources. The three lifetimes come from an abstract (OSTI/ETDEWEB record of Z. Phys. D 32, 31), read through an automated page reader and not checked against the printed paper. NIST carries A values for six 5p4 - 5p3 6s lines (Ubelis & Berzinsh); nothing better was found. Abundances: NIST isotopic compositions (120Te 0.09(1) %, 130Te 34.08(62) %). Third pass (2026-10-02): added the 6s 3S1 and 6s 5S2 lifetimes, the a 5P1 lifetime (identified through the excitation wavelengths printed on p. 32 of Zerne et al.), 123,125Te hyperfine constants and the 214 nm isotope shifts of 120-136Te from the open PhD thesis of R. Sifi (HAL tel-00252001, saved as pdf/Te_Sifi_2007.pdf). In that thesis A is the ground-level constant and A' the 6s 3S1 constant; isotope shifts are nu(A) - nu(130). Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: oscillator_strength_abs, isotope_shift_note, lifetime_alternatives. Fourth pass (2026-10-02): the four 7p lifetimes of Zerne et al. 1994 (128(11), 99(8), 82(10), 124(8) ns) were read a second time, independently, in the abstract on the Lund University publication record (https://lup.lub.lu.se/record/2259787) and agree with the stored values; the printed pages 33-34 are still unread.

levels.name: \mathrm{a}\,^5P_{1}
levels.tau_src: Zerne, Berzinsh, Svanberg, Z. Phys. D 32, 31 (1994), abstract (p. 31) and p. 32 (first two pages read in the publisher's preview): '7p 5P1' excited from 6s 3S1 at 591 nm and detected at 518 nm. Note: level identification derived here from the printed wavelengths: 46652.738 -> 63556.707 is 591.41 nm in air (591.58 nm vacuum) and 63556.707 -> 44253.000 is 517.89 nm in air (518.04 nm vacuum); the other NIST 5P1 level (b 5P1, 63669.944) would need 587.48 / 514.87 nm (air)

levels.name: \mathrm{b}\,^5P_{1}
levels.tau_src: Zerne, Berzinsh, Svanberg, Z. Phys. D 32, 31 (1994), abstract (p. 31) and p. 32: level called '7p 5P2' by the authors, excited from 6s 3S1 at 588 nm and detected at 515 nm. Note: level identification derived here from the printed wavelengths, not from the authors' J label: 46652.738 -> 63669.944 is 587.48 nm in air (587.64 nm vacuum) and 63669.944 -> 44253.000 is 514.87 nm in air (515.01 nm vacuum), matching 588 / 515 nm; the NIST 5P2 level 63610.819 would need 589.53 / 516.44 nm (air), which would be printed as 590 / 516 nm. The other three levels of the paper reproduce the printed wavelengths to within 0.5 nm with NIST energies (579 / 508, 573 / 504, 591 / 518 nm), which supports the identification. NIST (Morillon and Verges classification) labels 63669.944 'b 5P1' (J = 1) while Zerne et al. call the level 5P2: J assignment in conflict, see 'conflicts'
